feedback: If the string is read as a straight running sum (so IV becomes 6, or MCMXCIX is totalled incorrectly), highlight that a smaller symbol BEFORE a larger one is subtracted (IV = 5 − 1) while after it is added (VI = 6); then regroup into pairs.
If a learner writes IC for 99 or IM for 999, state the convention: subtract only I from V/X, X from L/C, C from D/M, so 99 = XCIX and 999 = CMXCIX (not IC or IM).
If D and M values are confused or a group is omitted, re-show the symbol→value chart and recount groups left to right.
When grouping is correct, name each chunk aloud (one thousand, nine hundred, ninety, nine) to confirm the decomposition.
activities.intendedInsight: A long, intimidating Roman year is really a chain of familiar subtractive/additive groups; each group reads independently, and only certain subtractive pairs are valid.
learnerActions: Assemble a year from symbol tiles including D and M, or read a given year such as MCMXCIX.
Split the year into coloured groups (M | CM | XC | IX) and state each group's value (1000 + 900 + 90 + 9 = 1999).
Convert both directions: read a Roman year into Hindu-Arabic, and write a modern year (e.g. 2024 → MMXXIV) in Roman.
Try an illegal shortcut such as IC for 99, see it flagged, and correct it to XCIX.
activities.title: Build and decode years with a symbol-tile decoder

feedback: If a date is misread, return to group-by-group decomposition before giving the full value.
Prompt the learner to justify why their grouping is valid (which subtractive pairs are allowed).
activities.intendedInsight: Roman year notation appears in the real world; the same grouping skill decodes authentic dates.
learnerActions: Look at dated monuments, film credits, foundation stones, or date inscriptions on clock towers that use Roman numerals (a clock face itself shows hours 1–12 rather than a year, and often writes 4 as IIII).
Decode each date into a modern year, saying how you split it into groups.
A guide or partner can read a date aloud and ask you to convert it, or ask you to write today's date in Roman.
activities.title: Read dates off real artefacts (guided)
